distractors: To check a text against the record and correct anything in it that turns out not to be true.
To cut a document down to an agreed length, deciding what has to go so that the rest fits the space available.
To turn a set of rough notes into a first draft, making the choices about structure and running order that nobody has yet made.
To rework a piece so that it argues a different position from the one it currently takes, usually because the decision it was written to support has changed underneath it.

To settle the vocabulary a group will use before anybody starts writing, so that two papers going to the same committee do not quietly use the same word for two different things. The work happens before the drafting rather than after it.
